column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:repl module
# A socket REPL server + client, implemented IN AQL (lang/go/modules/
# repl.go's preamble) over aql:net's lines codec — the first networking
# verification app. Each received line is evaluated in a sandboxed
# sub-engine against the session's accumulated history; the reply is
# the rendered result or an "error: …" line.
# §1  serve / close — start a REPL listener on an ephemeral port, stop it

column3: Repl.serve binds a listener; Repl.close stops it

column1: # §2  connect / eval — a full client round-trip (evaluate, then reuse a
#     definition from the session history; errors come back as text)

import "aql:repl" import "aql:net" def l (Repl.serve {port: 0}) def a (Net.addr l) def e (Repl.connect (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) def r (Repl.eval e "1 add 2") Repl.close e; Repl.close l; r
column3: Repl.connect dials; Repl.eval evaluates one line remotely

column1: import "aql:repl" import "aql:net" def l (Repl.serve {port: 0}) def a (Net.addr l) def e (Repl.connect (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) Repl.eval e "def x 21" drop def r (Repl.eval e "x mul 2") Repl.close e; Repl.close l; r
column3: definitions persist across lines (session history replay)

column1: import "aql:repl" import "aql:net" def l (Repl.serve {port: 0}) def a (Net.addr l) def e (Repl.connect (join "" ["127.0.0.1:" (convert String a.port)])) def r (Repl.eval e "no-such-thing") Repl.close e; Repl.close l; def rb (convert Bytes r) def r6 (slice 0 6 rb) def out (convert String r6) out eq "error:"
column3: a bad line replies with an error line instead of killing the connection
